thread.title: U.S. Congress hearing addresses North Korea human rights as core agenda
thread.title_full: U.S. Congress hearing addresses North Korea human rights as core agenda

author: m. y. simpkins
title: U.S. Congress hearing addresses North Korea human rights as core agenda
text:
The Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission held a hearing on North Korean human rights on April 28, with U.S. Representative Chris Smith serving as chair. Smith said at the hearing that “North Korea is one of the most oppressive regimes in the world” and described its system as a “horrifying system of repression unimaginable for decades,” citing torture, deprivation of freedoms, surveillance, arbitrary detention, and forced labor camps.
The topic matters because advocates say information flow into North Korea is crucial for change. Smith stated, “Information is the force that drives change, and any attempt to block it must be taken most seriously wherever it occurs.” He added that efforts by the regime to block information make it more valuable and powerful.
Suzanne Scholte, chair of the Defense Forum on North Korea, read testimony from Kim Ji-young of Free North Korea Radio about secretly listening to outside broadcasts at age 13. Scholte said at the hearing that “the most powerful force to change North Korea is not military power but information,” adding that “information changes people, and changed people eventually transform society.” She also described this period as “the most challenging in the history of the North Korean human rights movement.”
Smith criticized recent measures by South Korea’s government such as suspending broadcasts to North Korea and abolishing its Ministry of Unification’s human rights office. He called these actions ones “directly affecting civil society,” especially groups led by defectors communicating with residents inside North Korea.
In an interview after the hearing with Voice of America (VOA), Smith said human rights issues were not properly addressed in past nuclear negotiations and argued they “must be an absolutely core agenda under any circumstances.” He indicated follow-up steps could include new legislation.
Chris Smith has represented New Jersey’s 4th district in Congress since 1981 according to his official biography . He was born in Rahway, New Jersey in 1953 and lives in Manchester Township as reported by Wikipedia . Smith graduated from The College of New Jersey with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1975 according to Wikipedia .

The topic matters because advocates say information flow into North Korea is crucial for change.
